_README: DEBT LEDGER, not an exemption list. Every row is a known atomic write -- a
temp created in the same function and renamed into place -- whose exception
path does not unlink that temp. Rows are EXPECTED TO DISAPPEAR as fixes land,
and scripts/check_atomic_writes.py FAILS on a row that no longer matches, so a
landed fix cannot leave a stale entry behind.
Baselined 2026-09-07, denominator re-derived 2026-09-11 against this
branch containing main: 61 atomic-write sites across 53 files, of which
30 across 26 files are dirty. Three corrections landed on the way here. One
ADDED a CLEANS_UP site the detector could not see at all (an f-string temp
marker followed by a pid). One REMOVED a dirty site: main #1609 rewrote
git_discard_guard._write_log_row to one file per flush, deleting the
size-trim that renamed a temp into place, so its row went stale and this
guard failed until it was dropped -- the ledger shrinking as designed. The
shape did not leave the tree, it moved into audit_jsonl.write_batch, where
it is cleaned on both exception paths and on success. One ADDED two sites:
publish-by-hardlink and a temp marker held in a module constant were both
invisible to the detector. Both read CLEANS_UP, so no row here changed.
Evidence the class fires:
~/.genesis/tmp9cis_fly.tmp, 0 bytes, on disk since 2026-05-24, in a directory
no reaper sweeps (disk_hygiene.sh roots every find at a named subdirectory;
tmp_watchgod.sh covers ~/.genesis/cc-tmp and /tmp).
AN EARLIER BASELINE OF THIS FILE HAD 49 ROWS AND WAS 67% PRECISE. The detector
then anchored on the verb alone, so move-aside, claim-by-rename, rotate and
quarantine shapes were admitted -- 16 rows where the first operand is DURABLE.
Following the guard's own remediation on those would have deleted a live
credential, a user's file and pending telemetry. The detector now requires the
operand to be a temp BORN IN THE SAME FUNCTION. A false row here is not noise;
it is a booby-trapped work item.
Adding a row needs a REASON in the PR that adds it.
